verdict.rationale: Resend's own docs describe idempotency keys that can be added to any email request so the same request is processed only once even if it is sent multiple times, which covers the core of safe retries after a network timeout. The evidence is a single-sentence summary, so the full guarantee the story asks for is not shown. Missing for 10: the idempotency key retention/expiry window, behavior when a reused key arrives with a different payload, explicit coverage of the batch endpoint and SMTP sends, and any independent or hands-on corroboration that retries never double-send.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can retry a failed send safely — idempotency keys or documented duplicate-suppression semantics guarantee a network timeout never double-sends a receipt

citations.quote: Include an idempotency key in any email requests to ensure that the same email request is processed only once, even if it's sent multiple times.
